fi-paracheirodon-axelrodi.title: Cardinal Tetra
fi-paracheirodon-axelrodi.summary: A brilliant red-and-blue schooling tetra for warm, soft-water community and planted tanks.
rows: Schooling. Keep a group of at least 8–10
Quality flakes or micro-pellets plus live or frozen bloodworm, daphnia and similar small foods
Easy for farm-bred fish. Wild fish are less forgiving of poor water
Rio Negro and Orinoco basins (Brazil, Colombia, Venezuela). Most are now farm-bred
notes: Looks best in a planted tank with fairly dim light, driftwood and some floating plants.
Good tankmates: other small tetras, pencilfish, hatchetfish, small catfish and peaceful dwarf cichlids.

fi-paracheirodon-innesi.title: Neon Tetra
fi-paracheirodon-innesi.summary: The neon tetra, Paracheirodon innesi, is a small characid from the Amazon basin in Colombia, Brazil and Peru, found in acidic forest streams. Years of commercial breeding have weakened the ornamental…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens, include other schooling fishes to provide security, and you'll be rewarded with a more natural-looking spectacle.
Omnivore. Likely to be omnivorous feeding on small invertebrates, crustacea, filamentous algae, fallen fruit and suchlike in nature.
The type locality was originally given as 'near Iquitos', referring to the city of that name in the rainforest of Loreto region, Peru, although the specimens themselves derived…
notes: Provided healthy stock can be obtained (see 'Notes') maintenance presents few problems although it perhaps looks best in an arrangement comprising a sandy substrate plus some driftwood roots and branches.
The addition of dried leaf litter would further emphasise the natural feel and as well as offering additional cover for the fish brings with it the growth of microbe colonies as decomposition occurs.

fi-phenacogrammus-interruptus.title: Congo Tetra
fi-phenacogrammus-interruptus.summary: The Congo tetra, Phenacogrammus interruptus, is a tetra from parts of the River Congo drainage in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Wild populations are endemic there, but most fish in the trade are…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Omnivore. An omnivore feeding on small worms, insects, crustaceans, algae and other zooplankton in nature.
Wild populations are endemic to parts of the River Congo drainage in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
notes: Ideally an African biotope tank with driftwood branches, floating vegetation and anubias.
However they will show their best colours in any well-planted setup with plenty of swimming space.

fi-hyphessobrycon-herbertaxelrodi.title: Black Neon Tetra
fi-hyphessobrycon-herbertaxelrodi.summary: The black neon tetra, Hyphessobrycon herbertaxelrodi, is a characid from the upper rio Paraguai in Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil. A ubiquitous aquarium fish since its discovery, it is…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens, include other schooling fishes to provide security, and you will be rewarded with a more natural-looking spectacle.
Omnivore. Likely to be omnivorous feeding on small invertebrates, crustacea, filamentous algae, fallen fruit and suchlike in nature.
This species appears to be widespread throughout the upper rio Paraguai in the states of Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, both north and south of the the vast tropical…
notes: Perhaps looks best in an arrangement comprising a sandy substrate plus some driftwood roots and branches, or heavily-planted planted set-up.
The addition of dried leaf litter would further emphasise the natural feel and as well as offering additional cover for the fish brings with it the growth of microbe colonies as decomposition occurs.

fi-hasemania-nana.title: Silver-tipped Tetra
fi-hasemania-nana.summary: The silvertip tetra, Hasemania nana, is a characid from the Rio São Francisco basin in Brazil. It inhabits creeks and tributaries away from the main river channels. Hasemania is one of the few…
notes: Adaptable and will do well in most types of setup, but is particularly well-suited to a heavily planted tank.
Oddly enough, aquatic plants are not a feature of its natural environment.

fi-hyphessobrycon-megalopterus.title: Black Phantom Tetra
fi-hyphessobrycon-megalopterus.summary: The black phantom tetra, Megalamphodus megalopterus, is a characid from the upper rio Madeira and upper rio Paraguai in Bolivia and Brazil. Most records are from the rio Guaporé (Río Iténez in…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens since this species forms temporary dominance hierarchies within which males compete for female attention, and therefore displays more interesting behaviour and better colouration when maintained in numbers.
Omnivore. Likely to be omnivorous feeding on small invertebrates, crustacea, filamentous algae, fallen fruit and suchlike in nature.
Native to the upper rio Madeira, a major branch of the western Amazon watershed in Bolivia and western Brazil, including its major tributaries the rios Beni and Mamoré, plus…
notes: Perhaps looks best in an arrangement comprising a sandy substrate plus some driftwood roots and branches, or heavily-planted planted set-up.
The addition of dried leaf litter would further emphasise the natural feel and as well as offering additional cover for the fish brings with it the growth of microbe colonies as decomposition occurs.

fi-hyphessobrycon-robertsi.title: Roberts Tetra
fi-hyphessobrycon-robertsi.summary: The ornate tetra, Megalamphodus bentosi, is a small characid whose type locality lies on the main channel of the lower Amazon at Óbidos, Brazil. It is very similar to a number of congeners, some of…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens since this species forms temporary dominance hierarchies within which males compete for female attention, and therefore displays more interesting behaviour and better colouration when maintained in numbers.
Omnivore. Likely to be omnivorous feeding on small invertebrates, crustacea, filamentous algae, fallen fruit and suchlike in nature.
Type locality is ' Amazon River at Obidos, Pará, Brazil ', which corresponds to the municipality of Óbidos in the lower Amazon basin, located on the river's main channel between…
notes: Choice of décor is not especially critical although it tends to show better colouration when maintained in a well-furnished set-up with live plants and a dark substrate.
A natural-looking arrangement might consist of a soft, sandy substrate with wood roots and branches placed such a way that plenty of shady spots are formed.

fi-hyphessobrycon-rosaceus.title: Rosy Tetra
fi-hyphessobrycon-rosaceus.summary: The rosy tetra, Megalamphodus rosaceus, is a small characid from Guyana, Suriname and Brazil, in river systems including the Essequibo and Corantijn. It is so similar to Megalamphodus bentosi that it…
rows: group of at least 6 of these, preferably 10 or more.
Feeds chiefly on small invertebrates in nature.
notes: A biotope setup would be very simple to arrange.

Use a substrate of river sand and add a few driftwood branches (if you can't find driftwood of the desired shape, common beech is safe to use if thoroughly dried and stripped of bark) and twisted roots.

fi-gymnocorymbus-ternetzi.title: Black Skirt Tetra
fi-gymnocorymbus-ternetzi.summary: The black widow tetra, Gymnocorymbus ternetzi, is a characid from the Rio Paraguay and Guaporé basins in Brazil, Bolivia and Argentina. All the fish in the trade are captive bred and unfussy about…
rows: Omnivore. A most unfussy, omnivorous species.
Rio Paraguay and Guaporé basins in Brazil, Bolivia and Argentina.
notes: It's an active species and prefers plenty of open swimming space, along with some quieter areas.

fi-pristella-maxillaris.title: Pristella maxillaris
fi-pristella-maxillaris.summary: The X-ray tetra, Pristella maxillaris, is a small characid native to coastal waters of Venezuela, Guyana, Suriname, French Guiana and northern Brazil. In the dry season it lives in clearwater…
rows: group of at least 6 of these, preferably 10 or more.
Carnivore / micropredator. A micropredator, it feeds mainly on small invertebrates in nature.
Native to coastal waters of Venezuela, Guyana, Suriname, French Guiana and northern Brazil.
notes: This mass-produced fish is adaptable and will do well in most tanks.
It does look particularly effective in a heavily-planted arrangement though, and can appear a little washed out in very spartan setups.

fi-hyphessobrycon-eques.title: Hyphessobrycon eques
fi-hyphessobrycon-eques.summary: The serpae tetra, Megalamphodus eques, is a characid with an enormous range through much of the Amazon drainage and the Río Paraguay. Very common in the trade, it is also sold as the 'jewel', 'red…
rows: group of at least 12 specimens should be considered the minimum requirement since this increases the likelihood that the fish will be distracted by each other rather than their tankmates but will result in a more effective, natural-looking display.
Omnivore. Likely to be omnivorous feeding on small invertebrates, crustacea, filamentous algae, fallen fruit and suchlike in nature.
notes: Choice of decor is not especially critical although it tends to show better colouration when maintained in a well-furnished set-up with live plants and a dark substrate.
A natural-looking arrangement might consist of a soft, sandy substrate with wood roots and branches placed such a way that plenty of shady spots are formed.

fi-moenkhausia-sanctaefilomenae.title: Red-eye Tetra
fi-moenkhausia-sanctaefilomenae.summary: The red-eye tetra, Bario sanctaefilomenae, is a characin from Brazil, Paraguay and Argentina, living mostly in clear rivers that feed the Pantanal. All fish in the trade are captive-bred in huge…
notes: Quite an adaptable species that will thrive in most well maintained tanks, although it doesn't like very brightly lit or sparsely decorated environments.
It looks excellent in a densely planted tank.

fi-hyphessobrycon-flammeus.title: Flame Tetra
fi-hyphessobrycon-flammeus.summary: The flame tetra, Hyphessobrycon flammeus, is a small characid from Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo states in Brazil. Popular in the hobby, it is bred commercially in several countries and also sold as…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens since this species forms temporary dominance hierarchies within which males compete for female attention, and therefore displays more interesting behaviour and better colouration when maintained in numbers.
Omnivore. Omnivorous, feeding on small invertebrates, crustacea, filamentous algae, organic detritus, and suchlike in nature.
Restricted to the neighbouring states of Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo in southwestern Brazil, although its current distribution is somewhat uncertain.
notes: Choice of décor is not especially critical although it tends to show better colouration when maintained in a well-furnished set-up with live plants and a dark substrate.
A natural-looking arrangement might consist of a soft, sandy substrate with wood roots and branches placed such a way that plenty of shady spots are formed.

fi-hemigrammus-caudovittatus.title: Buenos Aires Tetra
fi-hemigrammus-caudovittatus.summary: The Buenos Aires tetra, Hyphessobrycon anisitsi, is a characid from the Paraná and Uruguay river systems in Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina and Uruguay. A popular and hardy aquarium fish, it is also…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens should be considered the minimum requirement since this increases the likelihood that the fish will be distracted by each other rather than their tankmates but will result in a more effective, natural-looking display.
Omnivore. Probably a foraging omnivore feeding primarily on worms, insects and other zooplankton, as well as smaller amounts of plant material and organic detritus in nature.
Widely-distributed throughout much of the Paraná river system in Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina, plus the Uruguay watershed in Uruguay and Brazil.
notes: Choice of décor is not especially critical though it tends to show better colouration in a well-structured, ideally planted, set-up.
Filtration does not need to be particularly strong though it does seem to appreciate a degree of water movement.

fi-copella-arnoldi.title: Splash Tetra
fi-copella-arnoldi.summary: The splash tetra, Copella arnoldi, is a lebiasinid from the lower Amazon basin in Brazil and coastal drainages of Guyana, Suriname and French Guiana. It spawns out of the water: a pair leap together…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens, include other schooling fishes to provide security, and you’ll be rewarded with a more natural-looking spectacle.
A micropredator feeding on tiny invertebrates and other zooplankton in nature, especially at the water surface.
Type locality is given simply as ' Amazon ' by Regan and most modern reports state that this species is widely-distributed in the lower Amazon basin in Brazil plus coastal…
notes: Best kept in a densely-planted aquarium or paludarium with some overhanging vegetation, roots or branches important if you wish to raise fry alongside the adults (see 'Reproduction').
Floating vegetation is also useful since this species appears to prefer relatively dim conditions and spends much of its time in the upper part of the water column.

fi-crenuchus-spilurus.title: Sailfin Tetra
fi-crenuchus-spilurus.summary: The sailfin characin, Crenuchus spilurus, is a crenuchid from much of the Amazon and Orinoco drainages and coastal rivers of the Guianas. The only described member of its genus, it varies…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Usually kept singly (or a known pair when breeding)

Predator / carnivore. Chiefly a micropredator feeding on tiny invertebrates and other zooplankton with the stomach contents of wild specimens from Guyana observed to comprise Ephemeroptera larvae, copepods and ostracods.
Type locality is the Essequibo river system in Guyana but this species is currently understood to range throughout much of the Amazon and Orinoco drainages plus coastal rivers of…
notes: Best-maintained in a well-structured set-up, ideally comprising a sandy substrate plus some driftwood roots and branches.
The addition of dried leaf litter further emphasises the natural feel and as well as offering additional cover for the fish brings with it the growth of microbe colonies as decomposition occurs.

fi-hemigrammus-erythrozonus.title: Glolite Tetra
fi-hemigrammus-erythrozonus.summary: The glowlight tetra, Hemigrammus erythrozonus, is a small characin known only from the Rio Essequibo in Guyana. Hardy and inexpensive, it is one of the best choices for a newcomer to fishkeeping. All…
rows: group of at least 6 of these, preferably 10 or more.
Known only from the Rio Essequibo, Guyana.
notes: As it's commercially bred in such huge numbers, it is adaptable and will do well in most tanks.
It does look particularly effective in a heavily-planted arrangement, and can appear a little washed out in very spartan setups.

fi-hemigrammus-ocellifer.title: Head & Tail Lite Tetra
fi-hemigrammus-ocellifer.summary: The head-and-tail light tetra, Holopristis ocellifera, is a small characin from Guyana, Suriname, French Guiana, Peru and Brazil. Also known as the beacon tetra, it is hardy, inexpensive and one of…
rows: group of at least 6 of these, preferably 10 or more.
notes: As it is captive bred, it's adaptable and will do well in most tanks.
It does look particularly effective in a heavily-planted arrangement, though, and can appear a little washed out in very spartan setups.

fi-hemigrammus-rhodostomus.title: Rummynose Tetra
fi-hemigrammus-rhodostomus.summary: The rummy-nose tetra, Hemigrammus rhodostomus, is a characin from blackwater rivers of the Rio Orinoco and lower Amazon basin in Venezuela and Brazil. This is the 'real' rummy-nose. Most fish sold…
rows: group of at least 10 of these, preferably more.
Omnivore. Omnivorous and will accept just about anything offered.
Rio Orinoco and the lower Amazon basin in Venezuela and Brazil.
notes: A biotope setup would be very simple to arrange.

Use a substrate of river sand and add a few driftwood branches (if you can't find driftwood of the desired shape, common beech is safe to use if thoroughly dried and stripped of bark) and twisted roots.

fi-hyphessobrycon-columbianus.title: Red & Blue
fi-hyphessobrycon-columbianus.summary: The Colombian tetra, Hyphessobrycon columbianus, is a characid that appears to be known only from the Río Acandí in Chocó, northern Colombia. It is also traded as 'blue flame', 'blue-red' and…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens, include other schooling fishes to provide security, and you'll be rewarded with a more natural-looking spectacle.
Omnivore. Probably a foraging omnivore feeding primarily on worms, insects and other zooplankton, as well as smaller amounts of plant material and organic detritus in nature.
Appears to be known only from the Río Acandí in Chocó Department, northern Colombia, close to the border with Panama.
notes: Choice of décor is not especially critical though it tends to show better colouration in a well-structured, ideally planted, set-up.
Filtration does not need to be particularly strong though it does seem to appreciate a degree of water movement.

fi-hyphessobrycon-erythrostigma.title: Bleeding Heart Tetra
fi-hyphessobrycon-erythrostigma.summary: The bleeding heart tetra, Megalamphodus erythrostigma, is a characid from the upper Amazon basin where the borders of Brazil, Peru and Colombia meet. The best-known of three similar species in the…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens, include other schooling fishes to provide security, and you'll be rewarded with a more natural-looking spectacle.
Omnivore. This species is an opportunistic omnivore by nature.
Type locality is given as 'probably border area between Peru and Brazil ', and this species is native to the upper Amazon basin in the 'Tres Fronteras' region where the borders of…
notes: Choice of décor is not especially critical although it tends to show better colouration when maintained in a well-furnished set-up with live plants and a dark substrate.
A natural-looking arrangement might consist of a soft, sandy substrate with wood roots and branches placed such a way that plenty of shady spots are formed.

fi-hyphessobrycon-pulchripinnis.title: Lemon Tetra
fi-hyphessobrycon-pulchripinnis.summary: The lemon tetra, Hyphessobrycon pulchripinnis, is a characid from central Brazil, mostly recorded from the rio Tapajós basin. It is bred commercially in several countries, but the origin of the…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens since this species forms temporary dominance hierarchies within which males compete for female attention, and therefore displays more interesting behaviour and better colouration when maintained in numbers.
Probably omnivorous feeding on small invertebrates, crustacea, filamentous algae, fallen fruit, and suchlike in nature.
This species' distribution is somewhat confusing.
notes: Perhaps looks best in an arrangement comprising a sandy substrate plus some driftwood roots and branches, or heavily-planted planted set-up.
The addition of dried leaf litter would further emphasise the natural feel and as well as offering additional cover for the fish brings with it the growth of microbe colonies as decomposition occurs.

fi-moenkhausia-pittieri.title: Diamond Tetra
fi-moenkhausia-pittieri.summary: The diamond tetra, Makunaima pittieri, is a characid endemic to Lake Valencia and surrounding waters in Venezuela. It is usually sold as a fairly bland, silvery juvenile, and given time and a good…
rows: Endemic to Lake Valencia and surrounding waters, Venezuela.
notes: Quite an adaptable species that will thrive in most well-maintained tanks, although it doesn't like very brightly lit or sparsely decorated environments.
It looks excellent in a densely planted tank, where it will develop some really intense colours.

fi-nematobrycon-palmeri.title: Emperor Tetra
fi-nematobrycon-palmeri.summary: The emperor tetra, Nematobrycon palmeri, is a characid endemic to the San Juan and Atrato basins in Colombia. Virtually all fish in the trade are captive bred, and it is hardy and unfussy about water…
rows: group of at least half a dozen of these, preferably 10 or more.
Predator / carnivore. Likely to be a micropredator feeding on small insects, worms, crustaceans and other zooplankton in nature.
Endemic to the San Juan and Atrato river basins in Colombia with type locality ' Condoto, Río Condoto and Novita, Río Tamana, southwestern Colombia'.

fi-prionobrama-filigera.title: Glass Bloodfin Tetra
fi-prionobrama-filigera.summary: The glass bloodfin tetra, Prionobrama filigera, is a characid recorded from the Amazon drainage in Ecuador, Colombia, Peru, Bolivia and Brazil. It is told from the other bloodfin tetra, Aphyocharax…
rows: The upturned mouth and slightly keeled body shape suggest that this species feeds primarily on small invertebrates taken from the water surface in the wild.
Recorded from various sections of the Amazon drainage in Ecuador, Colombia, Peru, Bolivia and Brazil.
notes: This active, pelagic species is usually found in the upper water layers in nature and the aquarium should contain plenty of open space for swimming.
It looks particularly effective when maintained as a group in a well-planted aquarium with patches of floating plants.

fi-sawbwa-resplendens.title: Asian Rummynose Tetra
fi-sawbwa-resplendens.summary: Sawbwa resplendens is a small cyprinid endemic to Inlé Lake and its associated watershed in Shan State, eastern Myanmar. It is traded as 'Asian rummynose', 'rummynose rasbora' and 'naked…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Likely to feed chiefly on small invertebrates and other zooplankton in nature.
Endemic to the isolated mountain lake of Inlé and associated watershed in Shan State, eastern Myanmar.
notes: Perhaps most suited to a heavily-planted set-up, preferably with a dark substrate.
The broken lines of sight that exist in such a display allow it to display natural behaviour as well as helping to reduce skittishness.

fi-tanichthys-albonubes.title: White Cloud
fi-tanichthys-albonubes.summary: The White Cloud Mountain minnow, Tanichthys albonubes, is a small cyprinid from Guangdong and Hainan in southern China and from northeastern Vietnam. It appears to have been extirpated from White…
rows: schooling fish by nature and ideally a group comprising 10+ specimens should be purchased.
Predator / carnivore. Stomach analyses of wild specimens have revealed it to be a micropredator feeding on small insects, worms, crustaceans and other zooplankton.
Type locality is 'White Cloud Mountain, Kwangtung, China ', referring to White Cloud Mountain (also known as Mount Baiyun or Baiyunshan) a few miles north of the city of…
notes: Choice of décor is not especially critical though it tends to show better colouration in a heavily-planted set-up with a dark substrate.
The addition of some floating plants, driftwood roots or branches, and leaf litter also seems to be appreciated and adds a more natural feel.

fi-thayeria-boehlkei.title: Penguin Tetra
fi-thayeria-boehlkei.summary: The false penguin tetra, Thayeria boehlkei, is a characin probably restricted to the upper Amazon in Peru and the Rio Araguaia in Brazil. By far the most popular Thayeria in the hobby, it is usually…
rows: group of at least 6 of these, preferably 10 or more.
Predator / carnivore. It's a micropredator by nature, feeding on a variety of insects, worms, crustaceans and other small invertebrates in nature.
Probably restricted to parts of the upper Amazon basin in Peru and the Rio Araguaia in Brazil.
notes: This species makes a superb addition to the heavily-planted aquarium or well-maintained community.
A planted tank can of course be further decorated with twisted roots, branches, smooth rocks and stones.

fi-thoracocharax-stellatus.title: Silver Hatchet
fi-thoracocharax-stellatus.summary: The spotfin hatchetfish, Thoracocharax stellatus, is the most widespread neotropical hatchetfish, recorded from much of South America. It is told from its only congener, T. securis, by a prominent…
rows: Remaining close to the shore, it feeds primarily on insects; a study (Netto-Ferreira et al, 2007) [2] determined that 99.6% of the diet of this fish consists of insects, and the majority (87.6%) of…
The most widespread of all neotropical hatchetfishes; it has been recorded throughout much of South America including Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Brazil, Peru, Bolivia, Paraguay, and Argentina.
notes: Cover a good portion of the water surface with floating plants, which will help to make this flighty species less skittish.
It seems to enjoy a bit of current to swim against occasionally but some quiet areas should also be provided.

fi-boehlkea-fredcochui.title: Blue Tetra
fi-boehlkea-fredcochui.summary: Boehlkea fredcochui, also known as the Cochu's blue tetra, is a species of characin. Its natural range is in the Amazon Basin. It is commonly kept as an aquarium fish. [ 1 ] [ 2 ]
rows: Up to about 5.4 cm TL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-hemigrammopetersius-caudalis.title: Yellow Congo Tetra
fi-hemigrammopetersius-caudalis.summary: Yellow Congo Tetra (Hemigrammopetersius caudalis) for freshwater aquariums.
rows: Up to about 6.2 cm TL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-hyphessobrycon-ornatus.title: Candy Cane HY511 Tetra
fi-hyphessobrycon-ornatus.summary: Candy Cane HY511 Tetra (Hyphessobrycon ornatus) for freshwater aquariums.
rows: Up to about 3.4 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-nematobrycon-amphiloxus.title: Black Emperor Tetra
fi-nematobrycon-amphiloxus.summary: Black Emperor Tetra (Nematobrycon amphiloxus) for freshwater aquariums.
rows: Up to about 4.2 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)
notes: [ edit ] The emperor tetra is a placid aquarium fish and will be disturbed by more boisterous species.

fi-astyanax-jordani.title: Blind Cave Tetra
fi-astyanax-jordani.summary: Astyanax jordani is a species of freshwater ray-finned fish belonging to the family Acestrorhamphidae, the American characins. This fish is found in Mexico. [ 3 ] [ 5 ] It is known in the aquarium…
rows: Up to about 10.0 cm TL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-moenkhausia-costae.title: Costae Tetra
fi-moenkhausia-costae.summary: An active, peaceful schooling tetra from eastern Brazil with a dark tail stripe. Large groups swim in tight, coordinated shoals in a planted tank.
rows: At least 32 in (80 cm) long for a small school
Peaceful but can be a little nippy; avoid long-finned tankmates
Flake and granules plus frozen or live foods such as brine shrimp and bloodworm
São Francisco and Itapicuru rivers, eastern Brazil (well-vegetated margins)
notes: A planted tank with open swimming space and a dark substrate shows it off best.

fi-hyphessobrycon-procyon.title: Raccoon Tetra
fi-hyphessobrycon-procyon.summary: A recently described Brazilian tetra for the soft-water community tank. Peaceful and sociable, and males develop warm yellow-orange tones and longer fins.
rows: Very peaceful; males display at each other without harm
Groups of 10 or more with at least two males
Quality flake and micropellets plus small frozen foods (daphnia, mosquito larvae)
5.5–7.5 (soft, slightly acidic water brings out the best color)
Rio Aripuanã drainage, Madeira basin, Brazil
notes: A planted tank with open areas; leaf litter, peat or alder cones add the tannins it likes.

fi-inpaichthys-kerri.title: King Tetra (Royal / Purple Emperor Tetra)
fi-inpaichthys-kerri.summary: A small, peaceful Brazilian tetra with purple-blue color, sometimes confused with the emperor tetra (this one has an adipose fin). Bred regularly in the hobby.
rows: Peaceful; does not compete well with boisterous fish. Its fin-nipping reputation is mostly undeserved
A group of about six or more; fin-nipping mostly shows up when too few are kept
Easy: most prepared foods plus small live and frozen foods such as brine shrimp and Daphnia
Rio Aripuanã and upper Rio Madeira basins, Brazil; slow, tea-stained forest streams
notes: Sand, driftwood and some leaf litter make a simple natural setup.

fi-megalamphodus-sweglesi.title: Red Phantom Tetra
fi-megalamphodus-sweglesi.summary: A small red tetra from the Orinoco basin of Colombia and Venezuela, now placed in Megalamphodus. Very peaceful and bred commercially.
rows: About 1.4 in (35 mm) SL; FishBase lists 3.2 cm SL
A mixed group of at least 8–10; males spar for female attention
Omnivore: dried foods plus live or frozen bloodworm, mosquito larvae, Daphnia and similar
Upper and middle Río Orinoco basin, Colombia and Venezuela; small tributaries, oxbows and flooded forest
notes: Looks best over sand with wood and leaf litter, or in a heavily planted tank.

fi-paracheirodon-simulans.title: Green Neon Tetra
fi-paracheirodon-simulans.summary: A tiny blackwater tetra from the upper Rio Negro and Orinoco, related to the neon and cardinal. Its stripe is greener and its red is duller. All are wild-caught and can be delicate after import.
rows: About 1 in (25 mm) SL; FishBase lists 2 cm SL
Peaceful but too small and specialised for a busy community
Omnivore: dried foods plus small live and frozen foods (bloodworm, Daphnia, Moina)
Soft, acidic blackwater: SF gives 3.0–6.5; FishBase 5.5–6.0
Middle-upper Rio Negro (Brazil) and the Orinoco system on the Venezuela–Colombia border
notes: Heavily planted or natural-style tank with sand, wood and leaf litter; keep with tiny peaceful characins or small catfish.
